answer: Computed as asked: 16,244 Destroyed (>50%) of 45,433 footprints = 35.75%. But this is a biased, misleading 'loss rate'. The layer is every footprint within 1/4 mile of the Eaton and Palisades perimeters, so the 14,993 null-DAMAGE footprints (33%) mix undamaged structures inside the burn, buildings outside the perimeter (never inspected), and non-structures. Among the 30,440 footprints with a DINS record, 53.4% were destroyed (53.4% excluding 41 Inaccessible). I recommend reporting 53.4% as the loss rate among inspected structures and 35.8% only as 'share of footprints in the buffered study area', not as a true fire loss rate. Both fires are pooled; there is no fire field.
traps_or_caveats: Null DAMAGE is not equivalent to undamaged: the buildings layer extends 1/4 mile beyond the fire perimeters, and DINS inspects only structures inside/near the perimeters, so null mixes uninspected-outside-perimeter with inspected-undamaged (explicit 'No Damage' = 12,107 exist as a separate class). Treating null as undamaged dilutes the rate (35.8% vs 53.4%); at least ~2,147 nulls lie >~170 m from any inspected building.
Denominator choice is a judgment call; the two defensible rates differ by ~18 points. A proper rate needs the fire perimeters (not used here) to restrict footprints to inside the burn area.

Footprints are 2023 (mostly 2008-vintage LARIAC), so pre-fire and potentially stale; 'New' (600) and 'Modified' (2,000) records exist, and DINS structures not matching a footprint are missing from the join (structure-level, not parcel-level).

Non-habitable structures are counted as structures: 'Utility Misc Structure' (6,417), courtyards (289), solar structures (76), and 15,660 with no STRUCTURET (nearly all null-damage). Residence-only rate among inspected: 51.0%.
Destroyed is defined as >50% damage per DINS; the 'loss rate' is structure-count based, not value or housing-unit based (multi-family buildings count once).
Eaton and Palisades are pooled; no fire attribute, my longitude split (Palisades < -118.4, Eaton > -118.3) is approximate. Inaccessible (41) were neither inspected nor assessed.
DINS is a rapid field assessment (damage state as of inspection time, can be revised); duplicate BLD_ID (1) exists. GeoJSON has no CRS member (assumed WGS84).
